Read 2026-11-18 17:40 UTC from Langfuse (recipe in [[gateway-incident-lookup]], scripts in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/cloud-usage/`). Window 2026-11-13 03:00 UTC onward, Kenneth's 263741 excluded, UTC days.

- 3,448 requests with usage (3,409 Sonnet 5.5, 82 DeepSeek V4 Flash), 65 users, 88 user-days. 360M input tokens (94% cache reads, 5% cache writes), 1.48M output. Cost $123.66 by my price calculation (Sonnet 5.5: $2 in, $10 out, $0.10 cache read, 1h cache write $4, 5m write $2.50); Langfuse's own total says $97.03 because it prices the gateway's 1-hour writes at the 5-minute rate. Not checked against an Anthropic invoice.
- Per active user-day: input tokens median 0.72M / mean 4.1M / p90 11.7M; output median 6.7k / mean 16.8k / p90 47.7k; cost median $0.49 / mean $1.41 / p90 $3.99 / max $13.66; requests median 21.
- Heavy tail: top user 21% of spend, top 5 62%, top 10 75%. Without the top 3 users the mean is $0.84, median $0.31. Median user was active 1 day (mean 1.35), so these are early-curious-user numbers.
- Calendar days (users, cost): 11-13 6, $13.30; 11-14 12, $26.03; 11-15 17, $12.12; 11-16 19, $33.12; 11-17 18, $23.81; 11-18 (partial) 16, $15.28.
- Not known: which heavy accounts are staff or testers (264001 has 712 requests over 5 days, $25).

**How to apply:** quote these as the first-week read; re-run the scripts, don't re-collect. [[per-chat-cost-estimate]] is the older per-chat estimate.

**Verified against the Anthropic Console 2026-11-18 (Kenneth's Chrome, platform.claude.com/cost and /usage/cache):** Sonnet 5.5 billed $123.05 for Nov 13-18 (daily 13.40, 26.20, 12.27, 34.91, 23.93, 12.34 as of 16:45 UTC) against my $122.05 for the same cut with Kenneth's account added back, so my prices (1h cache write = $4/M) are right and Langfuse's $97 is wrong (it prices 1h writes as 5m). Use ~$123. The Console organization also holds Kenneth's earlier Opus/Fable tests, so read the Sonnet 5.5 column only.

**Cache (same sources):** 94.5% of input tokens are cache reads (the Console's 99.7% "read ratio" leaves writes out of the denominator). Bill by component: cache writes (1h) $73.7 = 60%, reads $33.9 = 27%, output $14.4 = 12%, uncached input $1.7. Each written token is read ~18 times. Daily hit rate 92.9-95.4%. Nothing abnormal except: 21 chats resumed after >1 h each rewrote the whole prompt (~$18.4, 15% of spend, expected with the 1h TTL); one unexplained full miss (user 264205, 2026-11-16 00:00 UTC, 63 s after the previous request, 187k tokens rewritten, $0.75); first requests of a turn write more (7.0k vs 4.5k tokens, 53% of all writes). A 5-minute TTL would net roughly $4-10 cheaper (depends on whether the cache expires at 300 s or ~420 s of measured gap; $17 if at 600 s), not a firm $4. The Console cache-miss-reason view needs the beta header `cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07`, which the gateway does not send.
**Cross-user prefix sharing (user's hypothesis):** real but small. 13 of 32 users' first-ever request read 6.2k/18.7k/30.4k tokens another user had written; new chats with no one warm in the prior hour read 0 in 11 of 11; with another user active in the previous hour 74 of 93 (80%) read something. [Corrected 2026-11-18: the first version said 55% because it counted tiny title requests, which carry no tools or system prompt, as warming the cache, and left out Kenneth's own requests.] Saved ~$1.08 (0.1% of reads); ceiling if every new chat hit it ~$8 (~7%). The hit rate is driven by each chat re-reading its own history (~110k tokens per request).

**Per message (2026-11-18):** 839 person-started turns from 59 users cost $123.66 all-in = $0.147 per message ($0.114 the reply, $0.033 app-started follow-ups, $0.0003 titles); reply turn median $0.058, p90 $0.237, max $3.08, ~3 requests per turn; by day $0.09-0.19.
**Cache settings, checked in code:** app (AnthropicCodec.cpp) puts breakpoints on the last tool, the system prompt and the newest user message; gateway (upstream.py CACHE_TTL = '1h') sets 1h on all of them. Official prices (platform.claude.com pricing page): Sonnet 5.5 $2 in, 5m write $2.50 (1.25x), 1h write $4 (2x), read $0.10 (0.05x), out $10. Shared-prefix reads come at four sizes (5,863 and 6,213 tools only; 18,700 tools+system; 30,384 whole identical opening prompt). Misses are mostly the first request of a prompt variant in the hour (24 of 25 zero-reads in the 30.4k family); ceiling from fuller sharing ~$5. Claude Code default TTL is reported as 5 min (1h via ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1) but only from secondary sources; not verified against an official page.

**Margin check (2026-11-18, from server settings and prod gateway config, not the web page):** "Expert" = alias slicer-1 = Sonnet 5.5, 5 credits per person message; "Standard" = slicer-basic = DeepSeek V4 Flash, 1 credit (unlimited on Workshop). App-started turns cost 0 credits. Credit prices: pack $10/500 ($0.02), Hobby $10/750 per month, Workshop $20/1000 per month, yearly $100/9k and $200/12k; signup grant 500 credits. Revenue per Expert message: $0.10 pack and Workshop monthly, $0.083 Workshop yearly, $0.067 Hobby monthly, $0.056 Hobby yearly. Cost per person message incl. follow-ups: mean $0.147, median $0.070, p90 $0.306; mean without the top 3 users $0.094. Cost is 147% of revenue at pack price on average; 39% of messages cost more than $0.10. Cost rises with chat length: $0.10 in messages 1-4, $0.33-0.39 from message 15 on. Ignores payment fees and unused credits.

**CORRECTED 2026-11-18 after an independent recompute by a fresh session (report: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_07c1bccb-4cc8-4915-a75c-13271eb0e163/cloud-cost-second-opinion.md`; I verified items 1 and 4 myself). These override the figures above:**
1. Total is **$124.65**, not $123.66: 42 web-search requests report 394,181 cache-write tokens with no 5m/1h split and my script priced only the split ones (priced at 5m, the whole org is $123.09 vs Console $123.05). Per message $0.149 all-in ($0.116 reply), median $0.060.
2. **A 5-minute cache is about break-even (-$2.7 to +$1.5), not a $4-10 saving.** I missed that new chats also lose the shared tools+system prefix after 5 idle minutes ($3-5) and overstated how much a request's streaming time inflates a pause (typical ~3 s). Not recomputed by me; I checked the logic.
3. Cross-user sharing saved **$4.5** (up to $11), not $1.08 (that came from the first script after I had found its bug; I never re-ran it). Ceiling for more sharing ~$4.7.
4. Per user-day (87, Sonnet only): mean $1.43, median $0.51, **p90 $3.30 interpolated** ($3.99 nearest-rank; heavy tail, quote ~$3.3). Resumed after >1 h: 33 resumptions in 24 chats, $19.1 (not "21 chats").
**Lesson:** reconcile any residual against the Console to the cent (the $1 gap was exactly the unsplit writes), and re-run a corrected analysis fully instead of keeping figures from the old script.

How to investigate failed AI requests on the JusPrin Cloud gateway (`~/Projects/tsd-enterprise/web_ent/jusprin/v2/`), worked out 2026-11-14.

- **Log lines:** `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND resource.labels.cluster_name="tsd" AND textPayload:"JusPrin v2 upstream failure"' --project tsdtechnology`. Each line has the status, the upstream request id, the format and the alias. No user, no reason.
- **Per-request records:** Langfuse (us.cloud.langfuse.com; keys are in the `tsdws-prod` deployment's env). `GET /api/public/observations?fromStartTime=…&toStartTime=…&type=GENERATION` (deprecated, v2 replaces it). `metadata` has `outcome`, `request_bytes`, `turn_id` (`p-<project>-c-<n>-m-<n>-attempt-<n>`), `request_kind`, `effort`, `alias`. This is what tells two people apart and shows Retry presses. `note` = a turn the app started itself.
- **Sentry server:** VM `sentry` in project `elegoo-backend` (us-central1-c), self-hosted docker behind Apache; the gateway reports to project 2. Serial console output (`gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`) shows container stops and starts. Apache answers 503 when the containers are down.
- **State on 2026-11-14 (check before relying on it):** the gateway sent to Sentry only upstream 401/403/404 and a failed chat save; the server's `LoggingIntegration` had `event_level=None`, so no log line became a Sentry event; the upstream error body was discarded; the desktop app had no remote error reporter at all, and showed an upstream 400 as "could not reach the service" with a Retry button.

Related: [[jusprin-cloud-provider]], [[jusprin-chat-capture-design]].

**Changed 2026-11-15 (tsd-enterprise 057ea6d412 on master; live only once deployed):** the gateway reports every unexpected upstream failure to Sentry with the provider's status, request id and error text, and the "JusPrin v2 upstream failure" log line is gone. Langfuse `outcome` then reads `failed <ExceptionType>` for reported failures, `upstream status N` only for 429/413/5xx, and metadata gains `upstream_request_id`. Check `git log` in tsd-enterprise before relying on either recipe.

**Changed 2026-11-18:** Langfuse's v1 `/api/public/observations` now answers 410 Gone. Use `GET /api/public/v2/observations?fromStartTime=…&toStartTime=…&type=GENERATION&limit=1000&fields=core,basic,usage,metadata,model` and follow `meta.cursor`. Each record has `userId`, `usageDetails` (input, cache read, cache write by TTL, output) and `metadata`. The same Langfuse project also holds ~1,100 unrelated `OpenAI-generation` records (model gpt-6-luna, other users); keep only names starting `jusprin-v2-`. Working scripts: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/cloud-usage/` (fetch2.py, analyze.py). See [[jusprin2-cloud-usage-per-user]].

All of the Claude API usage in the past two days came from ordinary JusPrin users chatting through JusPrin Cloud. There was no leaked key, no test run and no internal job. Spend was $45.29 on Nov 24 and $44.60 on Nov 25 (UTC), against $16–27 a day the week before. The Anthropic Console puts all of it on the `jusprin-prod` key, and that matches the gateway's own request records to the cent.

**Who used it (Nov 24–25, $93.33 in total, 37 accounts)**

| User id | Email | Joined | Cost | Chats / messages |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 264756 | javier.manjarres@gmail.com | Nov 20 | $18.90 | 10 / 91 |
| 264534 | coc63sylvain@gmail.com | Nov 18 | $14.61 | 16 / 49 |

| 264955 | edupereirasalazar@gmail.com | Nov 22 | $2.97 | 2 / 37 |
| 265148 | alinrzv99@gmail.com | Nov 24 | $2.75 | 2 / 31 |

The other 29 accounts used less than $2.40 each.

**What stands out**

- **None of these accounts pays.** Every top user is a new free account spending the 500 credits it got at sign-up, and none is staff. No paid plan has been created since launch.
- **Sign-ups did not rise.** There were 9–14 new accounts a day all week. The jump comes from a few heavy users. The top three accounts made up $48 of the $93, about half.
- **Very long chats are what make it expensive.** In the top three accounts' chats, a single request reached 610k–688k tokens. Most of those tokens are cache reads (a cheaper rate Anthropic charges for re-sent conversation history). Even so, each message costs far more than the credits charged for it. For example, account 265181 spent 120 credits, which sells for about $2.40 at the credit-pack price, and cost us $14.45.
- **Their credits will run out soon.** Account 264534 has 30 credits left and 265029 has 40, so those two will hit their limit shortly unless they buy more.

This is a lookup only; I changed nothing. Should I look into why some chats grow past 600k tokens per request: yes, or not now?

**Built 2026-10-29; cherry-picked the same day to local tsd-enterprise master (906752ee3e after squashing, on unpushed a22082b0cb) and local jusprin-newui (30ae01eae0, one commit: chat_key plumbing copied byte-for-byte from a08d17471f without prompt_cache_key, plus the header).** Originally (branches and worktrees deleted 2026-10-29 after squashing): gateway on tsd-enterprise `claude/jusprin-chat-capture` (6d10075718, worktree `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/chat-capture`, tests via docker compose project `chat-capture` with a ports-reset override; obico-server submodule must be at eb0f29c3 there). App header on JusPrin `claude/chat-uid-header` (on `claude/chat-history-cache`). Chat id = sha256(`<projectId>/<conversationId>`)[:32], not a stored chatUid. Trimming removal and the context-limit rule belong to the chat-history-cache programme (R3a done, R3b pending), not to this work.

Kenneth's decisions (2026-10-29):
- **Chat id:** the app sends its own random `chatUid` in an `X-JusPrin-Chat` header. The turn id (`<project>-<conversation>-<message>-attempt-n`) can't be split reliably, because conversation ids are `c-1` and restart per project.
- **No trimming:** the app removes history trimming, so the newest request of a chat is the whole chat.
- **Buffered saves:** keep the newest request plus its reply per chat in Redis, and have a Celery beat task write it to GCS once the chat is quiet. Kenneth called saving every request "pretty dumb".
- **Consent:** opt-out was decided, then removed the same day (folded into 906752ee3e): keep every chat; sharing for a reward is arranged case by case. No account field or toggle. Account deletion still deletes kept chats. **Superseded 2026-11-10:** Kenneth chose "opt-in first": production keeps no chats until the app and server have a per-person opt-in, because the published privacy policy (obico.io/jusprin-privacy.html) keeps data "only as long as we need it to provide the service" and promises no AI training without opt-in. The server code as built (`capture.enabled()` only checks the container setting) has no opt-in.
- **Retention:** kept until the person deletes their account; no age limit.
- **Blind write, no branches (2026-11-02):** `_keep_sync` stores the request and reply events as raw text, and a retry, edit or revert overwrites the earlier version. Kenneth chose this over keeping branch files, knowing rejected attempts are lost. `[json.loads(data) for data in self.events]` had thrown on OpenRouter's `data: [DONE]`, losing every Standard chat. Commit 7c69f331be on tsd-enterprise `claude/credits-ledger`, not pushed as of 2026-11-02. The design doc's Branches section is out of date.

State on 2026-11-10 (later the same day): Kenneth dropped the opt-in and chose a Privacy Policy clause ("We use your information to improve JusPrin", with opt-out by emailing jusprin-support@obico.io) and said "Turn it on now". Chat keeping is ON in staging and production: `REDACTED` set with `kubectl set env` on tsdws-stg/tsdtasks-stg/tsdws-prod/tsdtasks-prod (not `apply`: tsdws-prod runs 10 replicas, its yaml says 12). tsdbeat-prod moved to obi.4098 so it schedules `flush_jusprin_chats`. Kenneth granted `appserviceaccount-storage-lp` Storage Object Admin on both buckets. Verified on staging: a real gateway chat was buffered and the 16:30 UTC flush wrote `483/<chat>.json.gz` (test object then deleted). Production flush runs and logs "Wrote 0" until real chats come in. The ops repo manifest edits are uncommitted. The server has no per-person exclusion, so an emailed opt-out can only delete what was kept (forget_jusprin_chats). The live obico.io policy page still promised opt-in at switch-on time.

State on 2026-11-02: 906752ee3e is on origin/master and origin/release. No deployment's `env` on the clusters names `JUSPRIN_V2_CAPTURE_CONTAINER`, and neither does the ops repo, so capture looks off; a value from a secret via `envFrom` was not checked.

**Why:** Kenneth wants the stored chats usable as fine-tuning data later.

- The new policy text (Claude doc 3USmxZnqCvQGPC3Bx9rf5V, suggestions pending) still has to be published to obico.io; the JusPrin 2 announcement email serves as the notice.

Since 2026-10-30 (commit "Stop naming Orca to the model...") the app keeps each request sent in `<data dir>/jusprin/request-log/*.json`, newest 200, pictures replaced by their size, no headers, no responses or reasoning (Kenneth said no reasoning). Read that first; the steps below are only for chats from before it.

The app did not save what it sent to the model. To replay an older turn, rebuild it:

- Running build: first line of `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/log/debug_*.log.0` names the commit. Read `ProviderAgent.cpp`, `ResponsesCodec.cpp` and `AgentHost.cpp` at that commit, since the wire shape changed in b08a307459 (append-only record).
- Chat: `jusprin/projects/<id>/current-state.json`, `state.conversations[n]` (messages, `chatModel`, `plan`) and `state.toolActivities` (arguments and results, joined by `correlationId` to the message that made the call).
- Workspace block: `resumeCheckpoint.summary` holds it, including `sliceWarnings`; it is saved at the end of the turn, so check it matches the turn replayed.
- Left out of the wire: note messages, and the workspace block of earlier user messages. A note-started turn sends a user message holding only the workspace block.
- A fired skill goes only on its own request (`newest_once`), never on later requests of that turn. print-issues fires by itself on the first request after a slice with new warnings, not only on a chip press.
- Cannot be recovered: reasoning items from the turn's earlier responses, and a skill's picture.

Same day, found while testing the rewording: settings tools send the raw `def.tooltip`, which skips the translation catalogs, so 13 settings said "Orca Slicer" or "Orca" to the model. Fixed the same day by `with_product_name` in `OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp`, which says JusPrin (the word the person sees in the tooltip); guarded in `test_setting_display.cpp`.

content.text:
We did not underestimate the cost per message. On Nov 18 we estimated about $0.15 per person message, counting everything the message sets off. The days since then are in the same range: Nov 24–25 averaged $0.16. Spend doubled mainly because people sent about twice as many messages. A few very long chats made it worse.

**How I measured it.** I divided each day's Claude cost by the number of messages people sent on the paid ("Expert") model. The cost came from the gateway's request records, priced at Sonnet 5.5 rates. The message count came from the credit ledger, which records one charge per message. The cost includes the follow-up turns the app starts by itself (for example when a slice finishes) and the chat-title requests. Your own account is left out. I priced the requests myself, and the Anthropic Console shows the same $45.29 for Nov 24, so the prices used are right.

| Days (UTC) | Messages | Cost per message |
|---|---|---|
| Nov 13–18 | 914 | $0.144 |
| Nov 19–23 | 917 | $0.105 |
| Nov 24–25 | 579 | $0.161 |

Single days ranged from $0.08 to $0.19. Nov 25 was $0.19 and Nov 17 was the same, so Nov 25 isn't new territory. What changed is volume: 329 messages on Nov 24 and 250 on Nov 25, against roughly 170 a day before.

**Where the expensive messages come from.** A message costs more the longer its chat gets:

- Messages 1–14 of a chat cost about $0.09–0.12 each on average.
- Messages 15 and later cost about $0.21–0.25 each.

The cause is that the app sends the whole chat history with every request. It never trims the history, and you chose that so kept chats would be complete. Three new free accounts each kept a single chat going all day. Between their own messages, the app started many follow-up turns of its own. By the end, every request carried 500k–690k tokens of history, so each of their messages cost $0.34–0.60. Those three accounts alone were half of the two days' $93.

**What hasn't changed.** As of Nov 18 we already knew that an Expert message costs more than it earns. It earns $0.10 at the credit-pack price and costs about $0.15 on average, and that is still true. The new part is that long chats push the gap much wider, and nothing in the app caps how long a chat can get.

I added this re-check to my notes on cloud usage, so the comparison can be redone next week.
